content: MK cautions that the apologies must be treated with care as sources for Ṣāʾin al-Dīn's own views because of the duress under which they were written and his need to distance himself from Sufism and hurufism; he singles out the comparison with Ghazālī and Rāzī, the self-presentation as a standard Ashʿarī and the appeal to Pārsā's non-messianic orthodoxy as points to be taken 'with several grains of salt', and notes that Lewisohn takes the apologies at face value.
refers_to_primary: MK, Introduction, fn 44 (on Lewisohn and Morio)
